septic-tank-pumping.metaDescription: Septic tank pumping in Agua Dulce, CA for horse properties and hillside homes off Agua Dulce Canyon Road. Full pump-out and tank check by a local crew.
septic-tank-pumping.heroSub: Plenty of Agua Dulce homes have grown since the tank went in, and regular pumping keeps an older system ahead of the extra bathrooms and guests.
paragraphs: A lot of Agua Dulce houses look different today than when their septic tanks were first buried. Bedrooms and second bathrooms were added over the years, yet the tank out back is often the same size it was decades ago. More people and more fixtures send more solids into that tank, and the sludge layer climbs faster than the original owner would have expected. On a horse property with a busy household, the old rule of thumb for pumping may no longer fit. Measuring what is actually inside the tank is the honest way to decide how often yours needs service.

Getting a loaded vacuum truck to the tank is half the job out here. Driveways climb, wind through sharp turns and cross soft dirt, and some homes sit at the end of a private road in a canyon. Let us know about gates, loose horses, hay storage and trailers parked near the tank before we head down SR-14. Once on site, we open every lid, pump out the scum, liquid and packed sludge, then look at the baffles and the tank walls. If a lid is buried under wash sand or decomposed granite, we dig it out first and set the soil back afterward.

Our Lancaster company is locally owned and operated, so Agua Dulce pumping visits are planned around the drive and the property rather than squeezed in. After the pump-out, we walk you through the sludge depth, how high the liquid was running and anything that looked worn. A tank running high can be an early sign that the seepage pit or leach field is slowing down in the harder ground near Vasquez Rocks, and we will say so plainly. Call to schedule septic tank pumping in Agua Dulce, and we can set your next interval from what we actually find.

faqs.q: Our Agua Dulce home has had additions. Should we pump more often?
faqs.a: Probably. A tank sized for the original house now handles waste from every bedroom and bathroom added since, and the extra load fills it faster. A common guideline is every 3 to 5 years, but expanded homes with full households often need service at the short end of that range. If you are not sure how big the tank is, we can note its size during pumping and suggest a schedule that matches how the house is used now.

faqs.q: Can your truck get up a steep private drive in the hills?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes, but it helps to know the route ahead of time. Tell us about steep grades, tight turns, gates and any soft spots, especially if it has rained recently and the dirt is still wet. If the truck cannot get close, we can often run extra hose to reach the tank. When a spot cannot be reached safely, we will talk through other options with you before the visit.

seepage-pit-pumping.metaDescription: Seepage pit pumping in Agua Dulce, CA for older ranch systems in sandstone and rocky ground near Vasquez Rocks. Local crew checks how the pit recovers.
seepage-pit-pumping.heroSub: In Agua Dulce, hard sandstone close to the surface can slow a seepage pit for years, and pumping shows how much drainage the pit has left.
paragraphs: The same tilted sandstone that draws visitors to Vasquez Rocks sits under plenty of Agua Dulce yards, sometimes only a short way down. A seepage pit depends on the soil around its walls to take in liquid, and where those walls meet rock instead of sand, water moves out slowly. Pits dug into sandy washes usually drain better, at least until fine solids start lining the walls. Many of the pits serving older homes here went in decades ago, so the soil around them has been absorbing effluent for a long time. A pit that stays full is often reaching the limit of what that ground can handle.

Pumping a pit is about more than emptying it. We first check the liquid level against the inlet pipe, then pump the septic tank, because a pit that fills early is often being fed solids from an overdue tank. Next we pump the pit itself and pull loose sludge off the bottom. The telling part comes after, when we watch how quickly liquid returns. If the pit refills fast, the ground around it is likely saturated or sealed. If it stays down, there is usually some working life left in the walls. On sloped lots, we also look for signs that runoff has been reaching the cap.

Agua Dulce owners get a straight read on their pits from us. If the walls are sealing and pumping is only buying a little time, we will tell you and talk through what comes next, such as adding a pit in a spot with better soil. Finding that spot can be tricky when sandstone and sandy washes sit side by side on one lot. As a locally owned and operated crew, we would rather explain the options than sell repeat pump-outs. Call to schedule seepage pit pumping in Agua Dulce, and tell us where the pit cap is if you know. If nobody does, we can track it down first.

faqs.q: Why does my seepage pit in Agua Dulce fill up after a storm?
faqs.a: Rain is rare here, but a heavy storm can send water down slopes and washes and into the soil around the pit. When that ground is soaked, the pit has nowhere to push liquid, so it fills and the tank backs up behind it. Keeping runoff away from the pit cap helps. If drains stay slow after the ground dries out, the pit walls may be sealing, and pumping plus a recovery check will tell us more.

faqs.q: Is rock near the surface a problem for adding a second seepage pit?
faqs.a: It can be. Hard sandstone or rocky layers slow how fast effluent soaks in and make digging harder, so placement matters. A second pit usually works best where the ground is sandier, and a soil evaluation may be needed to confirm it. Los Angeles County Environmental Health may have requirements for new pits, so ask them early. We can look at the lot and help you understand which areas look more promising.

septic-inspection.metaDescription: Septic inspections in Agua Dulce, CA for ranch and horse property sales and expanded homes. Tank, baffles and seepage pit or field checked locally.
septic-inspection.heroSub: Buying a horse property in Agua Dulce means buying its septic system too, and an inspection shows whether that system still matches the house.
paragraphs: Homes in Agua Dulce often come with horse facilities, outbuildings and a long list of changes made by past owners. What rarely comes with them is a clear record of the septic system. A buyer may not know if the tank is concrete or steel, how many seepage pits there are, or whether the system was ever enlarged when a bedroom wing went up. An inspection answers those questions before escrow closes. It also tells a seller what a buyer's inspector is likely to find, which is much easier to deal with early than in the final stretch of a sale.

On inspection day, we open the tank, measure the sludge and scum, and check the baffles and walls. Water runs through the house fixtures so we can watch flow reaching the tank and see whether anything comes back from the outlet. Then we move to the disposal area. In Agua Dulce, that might be a seepage pit set into sandy wash soil or a leach field on a slope, where wet spots tend to show up on the downhill side. Hard ground near the surface can make a field look fine in a dry summer, so we also ask how it behaved after past storms.

Buyers, sellers and agents on Agua Dulce sales can count on a locally owned and operated crew that knows the area. Give us the escrow dates and directions to the property, including gate details and notes about the driveway. Leave the tank unpumped before the visit so we can see how the system has really been working. When we finish, you receive a written summary in plain language. Los Angeles County may have its own requirements for some sales or for additions, and we can help you understand what may apply. Call to book a septic inspection in Agua Dulce.

faqs.q: The house was added onto. Will the inspection show if the septic system is too small?
faqs.a: It can raise the question. We note the tank size when we can confirm it, look at how much solids have built up, and check for signs the disposal area is overloaded, like a high liquid level or wet ground. If the home now has more bedrooms than the system was likely designed for, we will point that out. Los Angeles County Environmental Health may have records or requirements that apply to additions.

faqs.q: Do you inspect seepage pits on hillside lots near Vasquez Rocks?
faqs.a: Yes. We find the pit cap, check the liquid level against the inlet, and look for signs of overflow or of runoff reaching the cap from higher ground. Rocky soil near the sandstone can slow drainage, so a pit there may behave differently than one dug into a sandy wash. If the pit needs pumping to judge its condition, we can usually handle that during the same visit after recording what we see.

septic-repair.metaDescription: Septic system repair in Agua Dulce, CA for cracked lids, broken baffles and lines exposed by hillside runoff. A local crew finds the cause first.
septic-repair.heroSub: On Agua Dulce hillsides, runoff and heavy horse trailers can damage septic parts, and we track down the failed piece before anything gets dug up.
paragraphs: Many Agua Dulce septic repairs start with the land itself. When a rare heavy storm sends water racing down a slope, it can strip away the soil covering a septic line, leaving pipe shallow or even exposed. Once that happens, the sun, the cold nights and anything rolling over it take a toll. Joints separate, sections crack, and the flow from the house to the tank or from the tank to the pit starts leaking. Horse trailers, hay deliveries and equipment moving across a property can also crack lids and crush pipes that never had much cover over them.

Inside the tank, age is the usual story. Many systems here went in decades ago, and concrete baffles slowly break down from the gases in the tank. A broken outlet baffle lets scum flow straight to the seepage pit or leach field, which is a costly way to lose a disposal area that may already be fighting sandstone and rocky ground. We open the tank, check the liquid level and the baffles, and run a camera through a suspect line when it helps. You hear what failed and get a quote before any digging starts.

After a repair on a slope, we pay attention to what caused it. That may mean regrading so runoff passes around the line instead of over it, adding cover over a shallow pipe, or moving the spot where trailers park. As a locally owned and operated business, we would rather fix the one part that failed than sell you work you do not need. Some repairs may involve Los Angeles County requirements, and we can help you understand what may apply. Call to schedule septic system repair in Agua Dulce and describe what you have noticed so far.

faqs.q: A storm washed out the soil over my septic line. Is that urgent?
faqs.a: It is worth dealing with soon. A pipe with little or no cover is easier to crack, can shift out of alignment and may leak where people and animals walk. Keep horses, vehicles and kids off the area, and do not simply pile loose fill over a damaged section. We can check the pipe, repair any broken joints and help you redirect runoff so the next storm does not repeat the damage.

faqs.q: Can heavy horse trailers damage my septic tank?
faqs.a: Yes. Standard tank lids and many older tank tops are not built for vehicle weight, and a loaded trailer or truck can crack a lid, a riser or the tank itself. Lines between the tank and the pit or field are vulnerable too. If you are not sure where the system runs, we can locate it so you can keep parking and turnaround areas clear. Damaged lids and pipe sections can usually be repaired.

leach-field-repair.metaDescription: Leach field repair in Agua Dulce, CA for sloped fields with wet spots downhill and sandstone that slows drainage. Local crew finds the cause first.
leach-field-repair.heroSub: A leach field on an Agua Dulce slope can soak the lower trenches while the upper ones sit dry, and fixing it starts with finding out why.
paragraphs: Gravity does not always help a leach field in Agua Dulce. On sloped lots, effluent tends to run toward the lowest trench, so the downhill end carries most of the load while the upper lines see very little. That is often where a soggy patch or sewage odor first shows up. A distribution box that has settled or tilted makes the imbalance worse. Add a rocky layer or sandstone under the trenches, and water has even fewer places to go. Uneven loading is one of the most common reasons a field here starts to fail long before it should.

We begin at the tank, since an overfull tank or a broken outlet baffle may be pushing solids into the field. Then we open the distribution box and check whether it is level and splitting flow the way it should. Probing along the trenches shows which ones are saturated, and a camera can find crushed or clogged laterals. Depending on the findings, the fix might be leveling the box, jetting lines, letting an overloaded section rest, or adding trenches in a sandier part of the lot. Each option is explained in terms of your slope and soil before work starts.

Runoff is the other piece. A rare heavy storm can pour water down the hill onto the field and soak it from above, so grading and drainage around the trenches are part of the repair. Keep horses and trailers off the field, and fence off any spot where effluent is surfacing until the work is done. Larger field work may involve Los Angeles County review, and we can help you understand what that may look like for your lot. We are locally owned and operated, and you can call to schedule leach field repair in Agua Dulce.

faqs.q: Why is only the bottom of my leach field wet?
faqs.a: On a slope, effluent naturally flows toward the lowest trench, especially if the distribution box has shifted or was never set to split flow evenly. That lower section ends up overloaded while the higher trenches stay dry. Leveling or replacing the box, adding flow control, or reworking the layout can spread the load. We probe the trenches to confirm which ones are saturated before recommending a fix.

faqs.q: Can a leach field work in rocky Agua Dulce ground?
faqs.a: It can, but placement matters a great deal. Sandstone and rocky layers slow how fast effluent soaks in, so trenches set over rock may saturate while a sandier area a short distance away drains well. A soil evaluation may be needed before adding or moving trenches, and Los Angeles County Environmental Health may set requirements for that work. We can walk the lot with you and point out the more workable areas.

septic-installation.metaDescription: Septic installation and replacement in Agua Dulce, CA for hillside lots and ranch homes where sandstone, washes and slope shape the design.
septic-installation.heroSub: Planning a new system in Agua Dulce means working with slopes, sandy washes and hard sandstone, and we help you find a layout that suits the lot.
paragraphs: Two spots on the same Agua Dulce parcel can behave like different properties. A sandy wash may drain quickly, while ground a short walk away sits on sandstone that barely takes water. That is why soil testing usually comes first on any new system or replacement here. The results help decide between a leach field and one or more seepage pits, and where each could go. Slope adds another layer, since trenches need to follow the contour and storm runoff has to be kept off them. Getting these decisions right shapes how the system holds up for years.

Replacement is common on older ranch homes where the original tank and pit have simply worn out, or where the house has grown and the system never did. In those cases, sizing for the home as it is lived in today matters more than matching the old layout. Los Angeles County may require a design, review and inspections, and steps can vary by lot, so contact Los Angeles County Environmental Health early. Our part is to explain which county steps may apply to a hillside lot like yours and to work alongside the people doing the soil tests and drawings.

Access is part of the plan from the first visit. Steep driveways, sharp turns and soft ground can limit what equipment reaches the work area, and we look at all of that when we walk the property. On installation, we set the tank level on a firm base, connect the lines, lay out trenches or dig pits exactly where the plan puts them, and finish with risers so lids sit at grade. The area is graded so storm runoff moves around the system. As a locally owned and operated crew, we keep you informed at each step. Call to talk about septic installation in Agua Dulce.

faqs.q: Do Agua Dulce lots usually need a seepage pit or a leach field?
faqs.a: It depends on the soil, the slope and the space available. Sandy areas may suit a leach field, while a seepage pit can make sense where deeper soil drains better than the surface. Sandstone close to the surface can rule out some spots entirely. Soil testing usually settles the question, and Los Angeles County Environmental Health may need to review the design. We can explain the tradeoffs once we have seen your lot.

faqs.q: Our house was expanded. Does the septic system have to be replaced?
faqs.a: Not always, but it is worth checking. A system sized for a smaller home may be overloaded by extra bedrooms and bathrooms, and signs like frequent pumping or a slow pit point that way. Los Angeles County may have requirements when a home is enlarged, so ask them what applies. We can inspect the current system and tell you whether adding capacity or a full replacement makes more sense.

septic-risers.metaDescription: Septic riser and lid installation in Agua Dulce, CA. Bring buried lids to grade on ranch and hillside lots so wind-blown sand stops hiding the tank.
septic-risers.heroSub: Wind across open Agua Dulce lots keeps piling sand and dust over tank lids, and a riser with a sealed lid keeps access at the surface.
paragraphs: Strong winds sweep across open ground in Agua Dulce, carrying sand and dust that settle wherever something breaks the flow. Over a few seasons, a tank lid that once sat near the surface can disappear under drifted soil, gravel or hay scraps from the horse facilities. Older systems put in decades ago often had lids buried from the start. Each pumping or inspection then begins with a search and a dig, sometimes through hard, rocky soil. A riser brings each opening up to ground level and ends that routine, which matters on a property where the tank may sit well away from the house.

We find the tank and dig down to the openings we plan to raise, usually the main access and the outlet side. The tank is often pumped during the same visit since it is already open. We check the tank top, fit a riser adapter, and build the riser in sections to the right height, sealing every joint so sand, rain and roots stay out. Heavy lids are screwed or locked down. On horse properties, we place lids where they are easy to find but out of the main paths that animals and trailers use every day.

Think about how the finished lids should sit. A lid a few inches above grade is easier to spot after a windstorm, while one flush with the ground blends in with gravel or desert landscaping. On sloped lots, we shape the soil around the riser so runoff moves past it rather than collecting at the lid. We are a locally owned and operated crew, and pairing risers with your next pump-out saves a second dig. Call to schedule septic riser and lid installation in Agua Dulce, and let us know if the tank has never been found.

faqs.q: Will a riser keep blowing sand out of my septic tank?
faqs.a: A sealed riser with a tight lid does a much better job than an old buried cover. Joints are sealed so sand, dust and rainwater cannot work their way in, and a lid that sits a little above the ground is less likely to get buried by drifting soil. You may still need to sweep debris off the top after a strong windstorm, but the tank itself stays protected.

faqs.q: Can horses step on a septic riser lid?
faqs.a: It is best to keep them off. Riser lids are generally meant for foot traffic, not the weight of a horse or a loaded trailer, and an animal can also be spooked by a lid that shifts underfoot. If the tank sits inside a paddock or turnout, consider fencing around the lids. We can help you choose a riser height and lid placement that work around your animals.

grease-trap-pumping.metaDescription: Grease trap pumping in Agua Dulce, CA for restaurants, cafes and food businesses on septic. Full pump-outs and service records from a local crew.
grease-trap-pumping.heroSub: For a food business in Agua Dulce, grease that slips past the trap can end up in a septic tank and seal the pit or field behind it.
paragraphs: Away from city sewer lines, a kitchen in Agua Dulce is often connected to the same kind of private septic system that serves the homes around it. That changes the stakes for grease control. When a trap fills and grease passes through, it does not wash away into a sewer main. It hardens in the septic tank, thickens the scum layer, and can reach the seepage pit or leach field, where it coats the soil and stops it from taking water. In ground that already drains slowly because of rock or sandstone, that damage can build up quickly.

Restaurants, cafes and other food businesses vary a lot in size and volume, so no single pumping schedule fits all of them. A small counter selling coffee and baked goods may go longer between visits, while a kitchen with fryers needs closer attention. Los Angeles County Environmental Health and other agencies may set requirements for grease handling, so check what applies to your business. We open the trap or interceptor, measure the grease and solids, pump it out completely, and scrape down the walls and baffles so the full capacity is back in service.

Because Agua Dulce sits a fair drive down SR-14 from Lancaster, we plan grease trap visits ahead and line them up with your opening or closing hours. Each visit ends with a service record listing the date and what was removed, which is useful if an inspector asks. If the kitchen drains to a septic tank, we can also check that tank so grease problems are caught early. We are locally owned and operated. Call to set up grease trap pumping for your Agua Dulce kitchen, and tell us whether it has an indoor trap or an outdoor interceptor.

faqs.q: Our Agua Dulce cafe is on septic. Do we need to pump the grease trap more often?
faqs.a: Often, yes. A business on septic has more at risk, because grease that escapes the trap ends up in the septic tank and can reach the pit or field. Keeping the trap well below full protects the whole system. Your schedule should match your menu and volume, and Los Angeles County Environmental Health may have requirements of its own. We measure the layers at each visit and help you settle on an interval.

faqs.q: Can you pump the grease trap and the septic tank on the same trip?
faqs.a: In many cases, yes, and it can make sense for a kitchen that drains to a septic system. We would pump and clean the grease trap first, then service the septic tank and check how much grease has reached it. That gives you a clear picture of whether the trap is keeping up. Mention both when you call so we can plan for the time and truck capacity needed.

emergency-septic-service.metaDescription: Emergency septic service in Agua Dulce, CA for backups, overflows and storm-soaked seepage pits. Call and we will get a truck out as soon as we can.
emergency-septic-service.heroSub: When a storm soaks the canyons or sewage reaches the house, call and we will get a truck out to Agua Dulce as soon as we can.
paragraphs: Septic emergencies in Agua Dulce tend to follow the weather. Most of the year is dry, but a heavy storm can send water down slopes and through washes, soaking the soil around a seepage pit or leach field all at once. With nowhere to push liquid, the system backs up toward the house, and the lowest drain is usually the first to overflow. Older systems on homes that have been expanded have less spare room to begin with, so they tip over sooner. A failed pump, a clogged line or a full tank can cause the same mess on a clear day.

Call us and describe what you are seeing, along with directions and anything about the road in. After rain, dirt drives and canyon roads can be soft or rutted, and knowing that ahead of time helps us plan the approach with a full truck. Meanwhile, stop running water, keep kids, dogs and horses away from any sewage, and unlock gates if you can. Do not open a pump chamber or try to dig out the tank while the ground is saturated. If you know where the lids are, mark them so work can begin right away.

Once on site, we pump the tank or pump chamber to bring the level down and get drains moving. Then we look for the cause, checking the inlet line, baffles, pump and floats, and the pit or field. If storm runoff is soaking the system, we point out where the water is coming from and what might redirect it. As a locally owned and operated crew based in the Antelope Valley, we drive down SR-14 to reach Agua Dulce and get a truck out as soon as we can. Call us for emergency septic service in Agua Dulce.

faqs.q: My drains backed up after a storm in Agua Dulce. Is the tank full?
faqs.a: Maybe, but storm water is often the real trigger. When rain soaks the ground around a seepage pit or leach field, the system cannot drain, and wastewater backs up even if the tank was pumped not long ago. Pumping relieves the pressure for now. If backups keep returning after storms, the disposal area may need repairs or better drainage around it. We can tell the difference once the system is open.

faqs.q: What if your truck cannot reach my house because the road is muddy?
faqs.a: Tell us about road conditions when you call. In many cases we can park on firmer ground and run extra hose to the tank. If the approach is unsafe for a loaded truck, we will talk through the options with you, such as reaching the tank from another direction or waiting for part of the drive to firm up. Meanwhile, keeping water use to a minimum slows the backup.

septic-line-jetting.metaDescription: Septic line jetting and camera inspection in Agua Dulce, CA for long ranch-home lines, sagging pipe and clogs that keep returning. Local crew.
septic-line-jetting.heroSub: Long lines from expanded Agua Dulce homes can sag, shift and clog, and a camera shows exactly what is going on before anyone digs.
paragraphs: Lines on Agua Dulce properties tend to be long and to cross varied ground. A pipe might leave the house, run through a sandy wash, and reach a tank or pit set wherever the soil allowed, sometimes a good distance away. Sandy soil can settle under a pipe and let a low spot form, where waste sits and builds into a clog. When a house was expanded, new drains were sometimes tied into the old line at poor angles. Runoff after heavy storms can also shift shallow sections. From inside the house, each of those problems looks the same: slow drains that keep returning.

To reach the line, we find a cleanout or open the tank, then usually run the camera first so we know the pipe can handle jetting. High-pressure water scours grease, sludge and debris off the pipe walls and flushes it toward the tank. A second camera pass confirms the line is clear and shows any sag, crack or separated joint. The locator on the camera head lets us mark the trouble spot on the ground, which matters on a big lot where digging in the wrong place would waste a lot of effort and torn-up ground.

Leach laterals on a slope can be jetted too, which sometimes brings back an overloaded lower trench without new digging. If the tank is due, pumping it on the same visit catches what the jetter pushes downstream. We are a locally owned and operated crew, and we show you the footage so the next decision is yours to make with real information. Clear a path from where the truck can park to the cleanout, and let us know which drains slow down first. Call to schedule septic line jetting and camera inspection in Agua Dulce.

faqs.q: Why does the line from my Agua Dulce home keep clogging in the same spot?
faqs.a: A repeat clog in one place often points to a sag, a separated joint, or a section that shifted when soil settled or a storm washed away its cover. Waste collects at that low point and builds back up after each cleaning. Jetting clears it, but the camera shows why it keeps happening. If the pipe has a belly or a break, repairing that section is usually the lasting fix.

faqs.q: Can a camera show whether my old line was tied into an addition properly?
faqs.a: Often, yes. The camera follows the pipe and shows each connection, so we can see where newer drains join the original line, whether the joints line up, and whether a fitting is catching debris. That is useful on homes that have been added onto over the years. If a connection is poor, we can mark its location on the ground and explain what a repair would involve.

septic-tank-locating.metaDescription: Septic tank locating in Agua Dulce, CA for ranch homes and hillside lots with buried lids. We trace the line, find the tank and mark it for you.
septic-tank-locating.heroSub: On a large Agua Dulce lot with additions, outbuildings and decades of changes, the septic tank can be hard to find without tracing the line.
paragraphs: Finding a septic tank in Agua Dulce can take some detective work. Properties are large, homes have often been added onto, and outbuildings, horse facilities and long driveways have gone in over the years. The tank may now sit under a gravel pad, a patio or soil that wind and runoff have moved around. Paperwork from the original install is frequently missing, and a buyer may get little more than a guess from the seller. Knowing where the tank and lids are matters before pumping, before an escrow inspection, and before any new building or driveway work on the property.

We start where the sewer line leaves the house, often at a cleanout near the foundation. A small transmitter goes into the line, and its signal is followed across the yard with a receiver until it stops at the tank. That gives us direction and depth along the way. Rocky ground and sandstone can make probing slow going, so tracing first keeps the number of test holes down. Once the tank is confirmed, we dig to the lids, mark them with flags or paint, and measure their positions from fixed points such as the corners of the house.

When a home has been expanded, there may be more than one line leaving the house, or a line that changes direction under an addition, and we trace each one until the picture makes sense. You get a simple sketch to keep with your records. Many Agua Dulce owners pair locating with a pump-out or with risers so the search never has to happen again. As a locally owned and operated crew, we plan the visit around your property and its access. Call to schedule septic tank locating in Agua Dulce.

faqs.q: Could my septic tank be under an addition?
faqs.a: It happens. When homes are expanded, the new section is sometimes built close to or over part of the system, and the line may have been rerouted. Tracing the line from the house shows where it goes and how deep it runs. If a tank or line does sit under a structure, we will explain what that means for pumping and repairs, and Los Angeles County Environmental Health may have guidance on what is acceptable.

faqs.q: Do you need to dig a lot of holes to find the tank on a rocky lot?
faqs.a: Usually not. Electronic tracing follows the sewer line with a transmitter and receiver, so we can narrow down the tank location before digging. On rocky ground near the sandstone, that saves a lot of effort and keeps your yard from being torn up. We then probe to confirm and dig only where the lids are. Without a cleanout it may take a little longer, but most tanks can still be found.
